body.heading: Stars into pictures
paragraphs: Long ago, people looked at the stars and joined them into pictures — a hunter, a bear, a queen on a chair. The pictures are called constellations.
The stars in a constellation are not really close together in space. They only look like a picture from Earth, like dots on a page.

body.heading: Make your own
paragraphs: Scatter dots on dark paper with your white crayon or star stickers. Now join the dots with lines to make any picture you like — a cat, a boat, a dragon.
Give your constellation a name. The Great Sandwich? The Dancing Giraffe? Your constellation is yours, so the name is your choice.

body.heading: Invent the story
paragraphs: Every old constellation has a story. Make up a short story for yours. How did your picture get up into the sky?
People on the other side of the world see the same stars. Maybe someone there is inventing a story about them tonight too.

takeaway: Constellations are pictures people imagine in the stars, and you can invent your own with its own story.
materials: Star stickers if you have them
safetyNotes: This is an indoor drawing activity — enjoy real star watching only outdoors with an adult at night.
screenFreeExtension: Pin your constellation on the wall and tell its story as a bedtime tale.
